claims.claim: Row filters are SQL UDFs returning BOOLEAN bound with SET ROW FILTER ... ON (cols); column masks are bound with ALTER COLUMN ... SET MASK.
is_account_group_member returns true when the session user is a direct or indirect member of an account-level group; is_member checks workspace groups.
Attribute-based access control (ABAC) policies apply filters and masks centrally through governed tags.

concept_html:
Grants decide who can read a table. Row filters and column masks decide what each reader sees inside it. Both are SQL user-defined functions that Unity Catalog applies at query time, for every query, from every tool.

Row filter. A SQL UDF that returns BOOLEAN. Unity Catalog passes it the columns you name, and drops each row where the function returns FALSE or NULL.

CREATE FUNCTION research_prod.research_governance.respondent_filter(tracker_id STRING)
RETURN is_account_group_member('research_approved_analysts') OR tracker_id = 'TRK-PUBLIC';

ALTER TABLE research_prod.research_silver.nat_respondents
SET ROW FILTER research_prod.research_governance.respondent_filter ON (tracker_id);

Column mask. A SQL UDF whose first parameter is the column value. It returns the value, or a masked version.

CREATE FUNCTION research_prod.research_governance.mask_postcode(postcode STRING)
RETURN CASE WHEN is_account_group_member('pii_readers') THEN postcode ELSE '***' END;

ALTER TABLE research_prod.research_silver.nat_respondents
ALTER COLUMN postcode SET MASK research_prod.research_governance.mask_postcode;

Three rules:

  • Use is_account_group_member(). It checks account-level groups, which Unity Catalog uses. is_member() checks workspace-local groups.
  • Test group membership, never current_user() = 'someone@example.org'. A named user in a function is a hidden grant nobody reviews.
  • Keep filter and mask functions in a governance schema, so their owners and grants are separate from the data.

Your reference script uses CREATE ROW ACCESS POLICY. That is Snowflake syntax. Databricks rejects it. Where many tables share one rule, Databricks also offers attribute-based policies on governed tags.

title: Row filters and column masks in Unity Catalog
why_html:
The reference unity_catalog.sql was written with an AI assistant and never run. Its row-level security uses CREATE ROW ACCESS POLICY, which does not exist in Databricks. The deployment script stops at that statement, and the PII table goes live without a filter, because the grants earlier in the script had already succeeded. Every analyst with SELECT on silver can read restricted respondent rows until someone notices the failed step.

A SQL UDF with SET ROW FILTER, tested in dev, applies the rule where Databricks enforces it.
